# ConversationList

A list of conversations to choose from: each row shows the avatar, the title, when the latest message arrived and a line of it, and marks unread conversations with a bold title and a dot. The open conversation's row is highlighted, under the pointer too, and marked `aria-current`. The list is a single stop for the Tab key, which lands on the open conversation; Up and Down arrows move between rows, Home and End jump to the first and last, and Enter, Space or a click calls `onSelect`. Rows can group under `sections`, whose headers open and close them. A list of more than 20 conversations renders only the rows near the view, and the Tab stop and the open row, each placed where it would be in the whole list and measured as it renders, so a long list costs about what a screenful does. The arrow keys, Home and End still reach every row, and the open conversation's row scrolls into view. A long list's other rows are not in the page, so code that reads the rows from the page, and the browser's find in page, see only the rows rendered: read `items` instead.

```tsx
import { ConversationList } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/conversation-list/conversation-list";
```

## Example

```tsx
<ConversationList label="Conversations" items={conversations} selectedId={openId} onSelect={setOpenId} />
<ConversationList label="Chats" sections={[{ id: "pinned", title: "Pinned" }]} items={[{ id: "ana", title: "Ana Lind", section: "pinned" }]} onSelect={open} />
```

## Use instead when

- Use `ItemGroup` instead for a static list with nothing open, and `Tabs` for a handful of views that switch in place.

## Props

Type: `ConversationListProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: width, margins, grid placement (`w-80`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `density` | `"comfortable" \| "compact"` | `"comfortable"` | `compact` drops the preview line and uses a smaller avatar. |
| `draftLabel` | `string` | `"Draft:"` | The words before a row's `draft`, for other languages. |
| `empty` | `ReactNode` | `"Nothing here yet"` | What shows when `items` is empty. |
| `estimatedRowHeight` | `number` | The row height of the `density` | How tall a row is, in pixels, before it is measured: the first render mounts as many rows as fill the view at this height, and the space of rows not drawn is counted with it. Set it when your rows are shorter than the defaults, so the first view mounts no more rows than it shows; rows taller than it are measured and shift the rows below. |
| `firstViewHeight` | `number` |  | How tall the list's first view is, in pixels: a long list's first render mounts the rows that fit it. Set it when the list sits in a panel much shorter than the window; leave it out and the window's height is used, which is an upper bound. |
| `items` (required) | `readonly ConversationListItem[]` |  | The conversations, in the order they show. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | What the list is, for screen readers ("Conversations"). Required, so the list has a name. |
| `membersLabel` | `((names: readonly string[]) => string)` | `"group chat with"` the first two names, then the rest's count ("and 2 others") | What screen readers hear after a group chat's title, from its `members`' names, for other languages. |
| `moreLabel` | `string` | `"More options for"` | What screen readers hear before a row's name on its more button, for other languages. |
| `onSectionOpenChange` | `((id: string, open: boolean) => void)` |  | Called with a section's `id` and whether it is now open, when its header is pressed. |
| `onSectionsReorder` | `((ids: string[], move: ConversationListSectionMove) => void)` |  | Called when a `reorderable` section lands in a new place, with the ids of the reorderable sections in their new order and the move. The list shows the new order at once, and keeps it until `sections` arrives in another order; the app saves it. A keyboard move calls it once, on drop; a drag, on release. |
| `onSelect` (required) | `(id: string, event: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void` |  | Called with a row's `id` when it is chosen by a click, a tap, Enter or Space. A handler that takes a second parameter also gets the click, so the app can check `event.isTrusted` or `event.metaKey`; a one-parameter handler or a server action gets the `id` alone. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |
| `reorderLabel` | `string` | `"Move section"` | What screen readers hear before a section's title on its grip button, for other languages. |
| `reorderMessages` | `ConversationListReorderMessages` |  | What screen readers hear as a section is picked up, moved, dropped and put back, for other languages. |
| `revealSelection` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether a changed selection brings its row into view. Disable for an automatic restore that must retain the viewport. |
| `sections` | `readonly ConversationListSection[]` |  | The headers the rows group under, in order. A row names its header in `section`, and a section without rows is left out. |
| `selectedId` | `string \| null` |  | The `id` of the open conversation. Its row is highlighted and marked `aria-current`. |
| `unreadLabel` | `string` | `"Unread"` | What screen readers hear for an unread row's dot, and a closed section's, for other languages. |

## Native attributes

Also accepts the attributes in React's `HTMLAttributes` (`id`, `aria-*`, event handlers), passed to the rendered element, except those named on this page.

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `conversations`: Not a prop. The rows are `items`: `<ConversationList items={conversations}>`.
- `groups`: Not a prop. Headers are `sections`, and a row names its own in `section`: `<ConversationList sections={sections} items={rows}>`.
- `onValueChange`: Not a prop. A chosen row calls `onSelect`: `<ConversationList onSelect={(id) => open(id)}>`.
- `selected`: Not a prop. The open conversation is `selectedId`: `<ConversationList selectedId={openId}>`.
- `value`: Not a prop. The open conversation is `selectedId`: `<ConversationList selectedId={openId}>`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: ConversationList merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with its own replaces it.[^layout-classes]

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `AvatarMember`

One member of a group chat, as Avatar's `members` takes them.

```ts
interface AvatarMember {
  /** The member's name: their initial comes from it, and screen readers hear it in the group's name. */
  name: string;
  /** The member's picture. Until it loads, and if it fails, their initial shows in their hue. */
  src?: string | undefined;
  /** What their hue is picked from, when it should not be `name`, as Avatar's `idForColor`. */
  idForColor?: string | undefined;
  /** The letters to take their initial from, when it should not come from `name`. */
  initials?: string | undefined;
}
```

### `ConversationListContentTitle`

A conversation whose title is content, such as its name with emoji drawn as pictures (`<EmojiText text={chat.name} catalogue={catalogue} />`), with its name as text beside it.

```ts
interface ConversationListContentTitle {
  /** What the row shows as the conversation's name. */
  title: ReactNode;
  /**
   * The conversation's name as text: what screen readers hear in place of the title, and the
   * avatar's initials come from it.
   */
  name: string;
}
```

### `ConversationListItem`

One conversation in a `ConversationList`: its title as text, or as content with a `name`.

```ts
type ConversationListItem = ConversationListItemFields & (ConversationListTextTitle | ConversationListContentTitle);
```

### `ConversationListItemFields`

What a `ConversationList` row shows of a conversation, whichever way its title comes.

```ts
interface ConversationListItemFields {
  /** Identifies the conversation; `onSelect` receives it. */
  id: string;
  /**
   * A quiet tag right after the title, such as "AI agent" for an agent or "Guest": small and muted, not a badge, and
   * read after the title ("Halden, AI agent"). In a narrow row the title shortens and the tag stays whole.
   */
  nameTag?: string | undefined;
  /**
   * A muted name after the title, on its line, such as the team a channel belongs to: "Design
   * reviews · Launch team". Text, or content such as `<EmojiText>` to draw its emoji as pictures.
   * It shows whole or not at all: when the row has no room for it, the title keeps the room and the
   * where is hidden, never cut to a fragment; screen readers still read it. Leave it out where a
   * section's title already names it.
   */
  where?: ReactNode;
  /** A second line under the title, such as the group a topic belongs to. */
  subtitle?: string | undefined;
  /**
   * A line between the title and the preview that says what happened and where, as an activity
   * feed shows it: the title names the person, this line "mentioned you in Design reviews", and
   * the preview the message. Text, or content such as `<EmojiText>`. It keeps to `density="compact"`.
   */
  context?: ReactNode;
  /** The latest message, cut to one line. `density="compact"` hides it. */
  preview?: ReactNode;
  /**
   * The first words of a message the person started here and has not sent. They show in place
   * of the preview after `draftLabel` ("Draft:"), in the destructive tone as chat apps mark a
   * draft, so a half-written reply is visible from the list. `density="compact"` hides it with
   * the preview.
   */
  draft?: ReactNode;
  /** When the latest message arrived, already formatted ("9:41", `<RelativeTime>`). */
  time?: ReactNode;
  /** There are messages the person has not read: the title is bold and a dot shows. */
  unread?: boolean | undefined;
  /** A small icon before the title, in the muted color, such as a pin or a muted bell. Give it a name (`role="img"` and `aria-label`) when it means something. */
  icon?: ReactNode;
  /** Small marks after the title, such as a `<Badge>`. */
  badges?: ReactNode;
  /**
   * The row's mark, at the end of its last line under the time: a mention `<Badge>`, "in 10 min" before a meeting.
   * It takes the unread dot's place; screen readers still hear `unreadLabel`. Words show small and muted, like the
   * time. It keeps to the line's height, so the row stays the height of the others.
   */
  mark?: ReactNode;
  /**
   * The avatar: a picture's URL, or an element to show instead, such as an `<Avatar>` with the person's presence.
   * Without it the avatar shows the title's initials; `false` hides the avatar. A person gets their `<Avatar>`, a
   * group chat its `members` (with `avatar` as a picture the group set for itself), and a team or a channel
   * `<Avatar shape="square">`, so a group chat never looks like a channel. An `<AvatarGroup>` is a row of faces,
   * wider than the avatar: it warns in development and names `members`.
   */
  avatar?: string | ReactElement | false | undefined;
  /**
   * A group chat's members: the row's avatar is the group, drawn from their pictures or initials as
   * `<Avatar members>` draws it, at the list's size. Screen readers hear who is in it after the title.
   */
  members?: readonly AvatarMember[] | undefined;
  /** The `id` of the section in `sections` the row shows under. Rows without a section come first, before the headers. */
  section?: string | undefined;
  /**
   * The row's own menu, as `Menu` entries: what a right-click, a long press, Shift+F10 or the Menu key on the row opens, such
   * as Mark as read, Pin and Mute. It opens at the pointer, or beside the row from the keyboard, and focus goes back to the
   * row when it closes. A row the list stops drawing while its menu is open (scrolled far away) keeps the menu where it
   * opened. A row without one keeps the browser's own menu.
   */
  menu?: readonly MenuEntry[] | undefined;
}
```

### `ConversationListReorderMessages`

What screen readers hear as a section is moved, for other languages: `{label}` is the section's title, `{n}` its place and `{total}` how many sections show and can move.

```ts
interface ConversationListReorderMessages {
  /** @default "{label} picked up. Position {n} of {total}." */
  pickedUp?: string | undefined;
  /** @default "{label} moved. Position {n} of {total}." */
  moved?: string | undefined;
  /** @default "{label} dropped. Position {n} of {total}." */
  dropped?: string | undefined;
  /** @default "{label} put back. Position {n} of {total}." */
  putBack?: string | undefined;
  /** What the grip button's description says. @default "Press Space to pick up, then use the arrow keys to move, Space to drop, and Escape to cancel." */
  instructions?: string | undefined;
}
```

### `ConversationListSection`

A group of rows in a `ConversationList`, under a header that opens and closes it.

```ts
interface ConversationListSection {
  /** Identifies the section; rows name it in their `section`, and `onSectionOpenChange` receives it. */
  id: string;
  /** The header's words: "Pinned", "Recent". They also name the section's list for screen readers. */
  title: string;
  /** Muted words after the title on the header, such as "your folder". */
  note?: ReactNode;
  /** Whether the section starts open, when the list keeps its state. @default true */
  defaultOpen?: boolean | undefined;
  /** Whether the section is open, when the app keeps the state with `onSectionOpenChange`. */
  open?: boolean | undefined;
  /**
   * The header's menu, opened as a row's is: a right-click, a long press, Shift+F10 or the Menu key on the header, or its
   * "…" button. Pressing the header itself still opens and closes the section. A header without one is unchanged.
   * @example
   * { id: "team", title: "My team", menu: [{ label: "Rename" }, { label: "Delete", tone: "destructive" }] }
   */
  menu?: readonly MenuEntry[] | undefined;
  /**
   * Whether the person can move this section among the other reorderable sections: by dragging its header with a
   * pointer, by its grip button (Space picks it up, the arrow keys move it, Space drops it, Escape puts it back), or
   * with Alt+Up and Alt+Down on the header. Mark only the sections that are the person's own; the rest stay where
   * `sections` puts them. Pressing the header still opens and closes the section. See `onSectionsReorder`.
   * @example
   * { id: "favorites", title: "Favorites", reorderable: true }
   */
  reorderable?: boolean | undefined;
}
```

### `ConversationListSectionMove`

A section that landed in a new place: its `id`, and where it was and is among the reorderable sections only, in `sections` order.

```ts
interface ConversationListSectionMove {
  id: string;
  from: number;
  to: number;
}
```

### `ConversationListTextTitle`

A conversation whose title is text.

```ts
interface ConversationListTextTitle {
  /** The conversation's name: a person, a group or a topic. The avatar's initials come from it. */
  title: string;
  /** The name screen readers hear in place of `title`, and the avatar's initials come from. @default the title */
  name?: string | undefined;
}
```

### `MenuCheckboxEntry`

A menu entry for `items`: an on/off setting that stays in the menu when toggled.

```ts
interface MenuCheckboxEntry {
  type: "checkbox";
  label: string;
  checked?: boolean | undefined;
  defaultChecked?: boolean | undefined;
  onCheckedChange?: ((checked: boolean) => void) | undefined;
  shortcut?: MenuShortcut | undefined;
  disabled?: boolean | undefined;
  /** The id of the agent action it performs, set as `data-ax-action` on it, as on an item. */
  axAction?: string | undefined;
}
```

### `MenuEntry`

One entry in a Menu's `items`: an item (the default `type`), a checkbox, a radio group, a group, a submenu or a separator.

```ts
type MenuEntry =
  | MenuItemEntry
  | MenuCheckboxEntry
  | MenuRadioEntry
  | MenuGroupEntry
  | MenuSubmenuEntry
  | { type: "separator" };
```

### `MenuGroupEntry`

A menu entry for `items`: entries under a label.

```ts
interface MenuGroupEntry {
  type: "group";
  label: string;
  items: readonly MenuEntry[];
}
```

### `MenuItemEntry`

A menu entry for `items`: an action, or a link with `href`.

```ts
interface MenuItemEntry {
  type?: "item" | undefined;
  /** The item's text. */
  label: string;
  /**
   * An icon before the text, as a `MenuItem` shows one in its children: an `<svg>` drawn at 16px
   * in the item's color. It is decoration: screen readers hear the label alone.
   */
  icon?: ReactNode;
  /** Runs when the item is chosen, by click, tap or Enter. The menu then closes. */
  onClick?: (() => void) | undefined;
  /** Makes the item a link, through `OuroProvider`'s router link for an internal path. */
  href?: string | undefined;
  /** The keys of the item's shortcut, shown at its end: `["mod", "e"]`. It does not bind them. */
  shortcut?: MenuShortcut | undefined;
  /** `"destructive"` for an action that deletes or cannot be undone. */
  tone?: "destructive" | undefined;
  /** Shown, but cannot be chosen. */
  disabled?: boolean | undefined;
  /**
   * Why the item can't be chosen now, as `MenuItem`'s `disabledReason`: the item stays reachable
   * with the arrow keys, shows the reason as its tooltip and description, and choosing it does
   * nothing and leaves the menu open. It wins over `disabled`.
   * @example
   * { label: "Paste", onClick: paste, disabledReason: clipboardEmpty ? "Nothing copied yet" : undefined }
   */
  disabledReason?: string | undefined;
  /**
   * The id of the agent action this item performs, set as `data-ax-action` on it, so the component
   * that declares the action finds its control: `axAction: "mute"`.
   */
  axAction?: string | undefined;
}
```

### `MenuRadioEntry`

A menu entry for `items`: one choice of several, as radio items under an optional label.

```ts
interface MenuRadioEntry {
  type: "radio";
  /** Names the group: "Sort by". */
  label?: string | undefined;
  value?: string | undefined;
  defaultValue?: string | undefined;
  onValueChange?: ((value: string) => void) | undefined;
  options: ReadonlyArray<{ value: string; label: string; shortcut?: MenuShortcut | undefined; disabled?: boolean | undefined }>;
}
```

### `MenuShortcut`

Keys for a shortcut, as `Kbd` takes them: `["mod", "e"]` shows ⌘E on Apple platforms and Ctrl+E elsewhere.

```ts
type MenuShortcut = readonly string[] | (string & { 'Use an array: shortcut={["mod", "k"]}': never });
```

### `MenuSubmenuEntry`

A menu entry for `items`: an item that opens a nested menu.

```ts
interface MenuSubmenuEntry {
  type: "submenu";
  label: string;
  items: readonly MenuEntry[];
  /**
   * An icon before the label, as an item's `icon`, so the words line up with the items beside it:
   * an `<svg>` drawn at 16px in the item's color, which screen readers skip.
   */
  icon?: ReactNode;
  disabled?: boolean | undefined;
  /** The text of the item that goes back from the submenu in the phone sheet. Default "Back". */
  backLabel?: string | undefined;
}
```
